idiom_name: private static Map<Key, T> + private constructor + static get(key)
implementation_notes: TypeScript keeps the classic shape but makes it type-safe: a private static readonly Map<Key, T>, a private constructor, and a static get(key) doing the has/check/set dance, with Key as a string union or branded type so a wrong key is a compile error. The Map is still module-scope state - per module instance, per worker - and the type system does not stop internal code from constructing new instances, so the discipline is 'one factory path'; where the app has a DI container with keyed singletons, register the keyed lifetime there instead of hand-rolling the static map.
pitfalls: private is compile-time only: the map (and even the constructor) stays reachable at runtime through casts or bracket access, so a closure variable or #private field is what actually closes the registry.
The registry is per module instance: bundling the module twice, or importing it through two paths, produces two registries and two instances per key.
Map operations are unsynchronised; in worker_threads or SharedArrayBuffer settings the type system prevents nothing, and the registry is not shared between workers anyway.
